我觉得大家都欠新三国一个道歉，新三国的机制确实是真实存在的。 《杀戮尖塔2》从好评如潮到现在骂声一片，就是胜兵必骄，骄兵必败的体现。而为何官方瞎改呢，则是为了触发败兵必哀，哀兵必胜的机制叠buff，好评率必将回暖。 《杀戮尖塔2》一直遵循褒贬不一那就是褒了的机制。 《杀戮尖塔2》中国测试玩家泄露事件，也说明了内部测试——密谋必定触发泄露。 《杀戮尖塔2》该听取哪些玩家意见，一直在A0和A10玩家之间转换，这尖塔到底你是主还是我是主？ 《杀戮尖塔2》外国玩家反映问题回复快，国内f2反馈回复慢，可见时间流速不一样。 《杀戮尖塔2》作为卡牌游戏，调整的卡牌越多，做的就越完善，换句话说，改废的卡越多，游戏就越好。 这些都说明了新三国是一部跨时代的作品，只是因为太超前了，被一群无知愚民诋毁。

The pros: Starting off strong, everything is just better than the already great first game in nearly every measurable metric. Encounters are more polished, bosses are more unique, there's more variety because of the new act variants, the unlock timeline is more dynamic than how it worked in 1. My favorite improvement, if i had to point out just one, is the better build variety. I def felt in the first game that some builds were just objectively better than others, and always felt myself falling into certain builds just because they were the only ones that felt viable at higher ascension levels. In 2, largely because of the greater card variety, there's so much more to play around with and in my experience so far no single build feels fundamentally better or worse than another. the cons: It's hard for me to gauge the difficulty, since i don't have that many hours and was never really amazing at the first game despite playing the hell out of it, but i def feel like there's more BS than the first. Some elites are just run-killers for me, which sucks the fun out of good runs. Like i mentioned, i love the new cards and added build diversity. That being said, the sheer amount of new stuff can make it difficult to make a proper build early on, i've had a few runs where i just get a bunch of pieces of different builds i cant really put together. Then again it may just be something that i learn to get better at with more playtime, as i learn more about what cards there are and what i can start to set up with what. My other big issue, and the one which concerns me most, is the lag spikes. I mainly play this game on my laptop, which isn't the most powerful device but can run a few heavy games, and experience regular lag spikes every hour or so. They're not horrible, but very noticeable and i don't really understand why they happen, since the game is relatively simple and i more than meet the requirements. I'm not an expert on pc parts, so i've attacked my specs for you to judge. I am worried about how this game will work on mobile once it goes over there, as the first one did. overall, i recommend. Despite my issues it is still an objective improvement to the first, even in early access, and i'm excited to see what they add in the future.

[h1]前言[/h1] 杀戮尖塔，想必大部分人都不陌生，卡牌肉鸽里最高的山，鸡煲笑话更是火的出圈，游戏的创意工坊更是让这个游戏更加出名，蕾忍和蛊真人等出名模组，更是让人心生好奇，奈何想玩的游戏太多，所以可能就算买了，也没有玩的机会，毕竟终归只是单机游戏。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注U_U鉴赏家，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] [h1]游戏玩法[/h1] 《杀戮尖塔2》是一款卡牌构筑肉鸽游戏，继承前作的大部分角色，对怪物翻版，画风优化，几乎相当于重制版，但塔2确实比塔1火，因为塔2添加了联机，原本塔1较难上手的缺点，可以和朋友一起玩之后，变得不是问题，新版画风更是让很多人为之盛赞。 简单介绍一下游戏的玩法，可操作的角色有几位，分别有着对应的卡组，敌人攻击你防御，敌人发呆了攻击，然后可以自己开一些加buff的能力牌，然后你的目标就是击败一路上的怪物，没什么要注意的，就自己注意着运营爬塔就好，上手很轻松。 [h1]游戏评价[/h1] 虽然大家常常吐槽“东尼意思”“逆天更新”，但都会在给了差评后，诚实的打开游戏拉上朋友一起爬塔，所以也希望真路人不要因为差评错过这款神作，毕竟我在二代出之前就是个真路人，因为二代出了，所以还特意尝试了一代，之后就喜欢上爬塔了。 低难度之下算是最亲民的，玩家摸索机制、数值和卡牌，虽说也会感觉难度较高，但不至于无法上手，再加上不同变化的地图，这种新奇感让人着迷，而随着一次次通关，对东尼游戏的改动，更加清楚明白，便逐渐会变成又爱又恨的老玩家。 作为和一代本质上最大的区别，其实二代的联机做的并不好，怪物数值严重膨胀，甚至有些坐牢，很吃卡牌抓取，而且互动性严重不足，无色牌联机卡与队友的互动性实在是太差了，奈何拉上朋友一起蠕动通关带来的惊喜又是实在的，只能说希望多推出一些联机卡牌。 [h1]近期更新[/h1] 而近来本作终于推出了一项万众期待的更新，也就是创意工坊的上线，初玩的萌新不必担忧太困难的学习成本，因为可以打些推荐的Mod，老玩家也不用麻烦的逛其他网站寻找熟悉的Mod，我说早就该上线创意工坊了有没有懂的？ [h1]结语[/h1] 总的评价下来，我还是挺推荐的，可以看我时长，玩快200小时了，角色都推到A10了，游戏本身是足够优秀的，虽然会有更新内容太安东尼思维，难度不合理等情况，但游戏本身是不错的，玩着觉得逆天的话，可以适当打一些mod辅助游玩。

I wouldn't normally post an EA review this early, but the game is being review-bombed, so I'm weighing in. Ultimately, this is a super-satisfying title. It feels both comfortable and challenging. BALANCE & GAMEPLAY The game needs some balance work. It can be super-frustrating to own the floor, only to get whomped by the final boss. The devs have nerfed the fun stuff a bit too much; infinites are cool, and game-breaking is half the fun. However, the balance is actively being attended to, so I don't see it as an issue. THE ROSTER 3 characters have returned so far: the Ironclad, Silent, and Defect. Each has been tweaked. The Silent's poison has been nerfed, but she is arguably more interesting for it. Notably, the Watcher missed the cut. I think there's a reason for that. There are 2 new characters: Regent and Necrobinder. The latter is quite playable and introduces some interesting defence-based mechanics. Regent, OTOH, feels like playing Microsoft Excel and will probably end up about as appreciated as the Watcher. VERDICT (SUBJECT TO CHANGE) Even without final art, achievements, and a complete storyline, this is a must-have game. It just feels so good to be back in the spire again. Highly recommended.

我喜欢这个游戏，但我不喜欢这个游戏的更新方向。 这个游戏beta版测试的更新越来越向着所有角色公式化抽五打五发展了，所有角色严重趋同，找更高伤害的攻击，更高伤害的防御，然后想办法把它打出去。大部分在回合内试图“抽更多牌”，“加更多费用”的卡牌都在削弱。但是，抽牌和加费才能导向卡牌与卡牌之间联动，但制作组似乎不喜欢它们有太多的表现，也不喜欢让玩家打出有趣的combo。 类星体印牌重构王国资产养猪的思路也被堵死了，这个combo的达成难度其实是很高的。我觉得这个改动其实完全不会影响角色的胜率，但制作组只是单纯地不喜欢“我没设计过”的思路和combo出现。我觉得这是个不太好的倾向。我是一个储君玩家，我打了几百局的储君，在99.9%的局里打不出王国资产养猪的思路，但是这样的“小窍门”的存在，让我仍然觉得游戏存在些许我尚未发现和体验的玩法乐趣。它们被完全堵死真的让我觉得挺糟糕的。 还有删牌涨价、大量削减优质的运转和加费卡，怪物们奇奇怪怪的针对性机制，都让我感到制作组似乎希望所有玩家都必须去按照他们所想的一样“开能力然后抽五打五”，打出更多的“铁斩波”，而不希望玩家们用抽牌加费达成“卡牌与卡牌之间的联动”，这让我感觉每一局的体验都在逐渐地同质化。这并不是一个很好的倾向。 当然，联机卡牌的增加是值得好评的。但我们储君和战士居然比其它三个角色少一张联机牌，这~不~公~平~，请给我们储君和战士补上这些联机牌谢谢。

I wanted to give this game some time since it's Early Access, but the direction for the last few updates has been pretty clear, and I think the developers are, for some reason, intentionally creating the most boring and frustrating roguelike deckbuilder experience. The crux of the problem for months now has been the third boss slot in Act 3. The Queen and the Test Subject are broadly fine. Test Subject in particular is a threatening final boss that can still be reasonably accounted for in both deckbuilding and your strategy within the fight. Queen is maybe a little easy, but not a complete pushover. The third boss, however, has been a complete train wreck since the start and they've made several attempts to change it, up to and including *deleting it and replacing it with a new boss,* and yet at no point during any of these stages was it a fun, rewarding fight. At first it was way too easy, as it effectively did nothing. Then they kept adding gimmicks until it was a bloated monstrosity that had 3 phases it cycled between every turn, each with a unique debilitating debuff that punished certain types of deck strategies. The main problem here was that many strategies were hard-countered by ALL 3 of the phases, making those strategies effectively not exist within the context of the game at all, and the card rewards that lean you towards that path were just "pick this to lose the game" options. This problem got so bad that they just deleted the boss. So what'd they replace it with? A new one, Aeonglass, who did... absolutely nothing, just like its predecessor's first iteration. Just sat there throwing out attacks and getting hit, like it was a very large version of the floor 1 enemies. Obviously this couldn't continue, so they gave it a gimmick and buffed the ever-loving hell out of it. Now it's a massive HP wall that gains armor, nullifies debuffs, adds unplayable status cards to your hand every time you play X number of cards, and also has turns where it shuffles even more of them into your deck while increasing the damage that all of them do to you at the end of your turn if they're still in your hand. They managed to recreate the exact same problem as the previous boss immediately, and to an even greater degree. Doormaker (the previous iteration) was certainly annoying in its deckbuilding restrictions, but wasn't fundamentally that much harder than the other two bosses. For the last whole beta cycle and major patch, Aeonglass has both been incredibly oppressive towards deckbuilding on top of being astronomically stronger than the other two bosses. As a result, every single run from before you even set foot on floor 1, you are just thinking "how do I not immediately lose to Aeonglass." Every card reward, every relic, every event, every Ancient, all of the decisions you could be making throughout a run collapse into the singularity of Aeonglass insurance. And the worst part is that some characters get punished far more than others by this gimmick, to the point that several sub-"archetypes" within classes, like Shivs on Silent, or Souls on Necrobinder, feel like they're completely unpickable from the start. Is the boss unbeatable? No. Should the final boss not require any deckbuilding consideration? Also no. But is the game fun when every decision you make through an entire 45min-1hr run is solely through the lens of: if I pick this, do I die to Aeonglass? Also no. Not even close. The start of a run in a roguelike is supposed to be the most magical part. You're back to square 1 with the entire game's branching possibilities at your fingertips. Maybe this run, I'll end up with a wildly different strategy and loudout than the last one. Maybe this run, an ability that is otherwise not great will end up being key to my success because I was presented with a unique challenge that wasn't there in a previous run. Maybe I'll get some kind of ability or relic that breaks something and I can diverge off into a new path that's completely different from what I was planning on. Slay the Spire 2's boss design takes this magic, and smothers it to death with a pillow before it can even get off the ground. Before I even begin a run, I'm already sighing at the prospect of building "the Aeonglass deck" yet again. Card rewards, relic rewards, Ancient rewards, they all lose their excitability because there is a correct answer for every run, and if you're not given the correct answer, it sucks to suck. This problem had already demotivated me from playing the game at all for this last month or so, and the new Beta branch update not only leaves Aeonglass as it is, but actually guts one of the few counters the fight had in one card on one particular class. As if the cardinal sin of Slay the Spire 2 is having a run where Aeonglass isn't the be-all end-all. The very idea of a card game final boss punishing you for playing cards is already dubious, but STS1 had one as well that wasn't nearly as oppressive, and nobody was clamoring for them to make Time Eater's 12 card limit into a 5 card limit, or to give him 100 more health. I had a lot of fun with this game to begin with, but if this is their design philosophy going forward, I'm not interested in seeing what they have in store for the future anymore. If Aeonglass is severely reworked or outright deleted like its little brother the Doormaker, I'll give it a second look. But as it stands, it's simply not enjoyable to play outside of unga bunga Ironclad decks.

I played 450 hours of STS1 and more on my phone (a lot more but it's not recorded). I absolutely love STS1 and I see a ton of potential in 2, which is why I feel so bad about leaving this review. It makes me wish for a 'neutral' review option, but that doesn't exist so here we are. STS2 has a problem. It's small, it's sneaky, and realistically it also existed in Spire 1, but it wasn't bad enough to make me write a review for that game. Basically, since 1, STS2 has less floors, far more cards, and a lot more enemies that don't just punish certain strategies but basically completely kill you for using them. Now, these things all need to exist (minus the less floors bit, add one or two to each act and it would help a lot) but the balance was super delicate. You add a few cards, make the enemies a little more single-solution-specific and tougher, and now you've got a really frustrating game. I have each character (minus Regent, because quite frankly I don't like him very much) at a10, I've gotten all characters on 1 to a20, so I would say I know at least a little bit what I'm doing. I feel at this point, unlike the first game, a lot of the time when I lose runs it basically comes down to one thing: RNG. Yes, sometimes I needed to take that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ aoe card for a specific fight (sow into exoskeletons in act 2 for example) or I needed to take another damage common to get through act 1, but with the card bloat, it is now very possible I'm walking into fights like Lagavulin Matriarch or Soul Fysh with no good answers into them. It is very possible I really if I needed a solution that scales was not offered one that works well into Aeonglass or something and now I just die because I wasn't offered the tools to win. A lot of the bosses now have way more RNG mechanics in their fights, like Vantom (who I see as a parallel to slime boss from STS1) giving unremovable statuses, and less off turns. Or Soul Fysh, who basically says if you draw 2 or more Beckons on an attacking turn, you lose. Or the Insatiable, now having an energy tax and draw tax built in that you cannot ignore or you automatically lose, regardless if your deck would have the output otherwise. Or queen, basically saying if you weren't offered draw (which except for clad, feels much more rare in this game) you are at quite a high risk of losing, or taking a ton of damage due to bound card RNG. A lot of the enemies feel way too strong, like Hunter-Killer, if you have the wrong build. Or, to a lesser extent, the floating statue guys in act 3. Pretty much all of the hard hallways in Act 1 except for smoke guy and triple seaslugs, and I guess sometimes the inklets. The ancient bonuses are way more varied, which on paper sounds good, and eventually it will be. Unfortunately right now it means I'm building decks with a bunch of random crap in case I see one ancient bonus act 2, for example I remove less strikes because soup, I need to add cards like afterimage or stone armor or p-strike in case I see clone, I need to add more 'generalist' stuff in case I see Prismatic Gem, I need to add lots of random cards in case of Yummy Cookie or Sandcastle, etc. Vaaku can sometimes brick, and a lot of runs with him it feels like I'm picking the least bad option. It makes me wonder why they removed the ability to skip the ancient relics, as we could skip boss relics in the first game. I think I'd almost never click it but it feels bad that the player choice to skip is now no longer present. Basically, what I'm saying is, because there is less floors in the game, everything has been tuned up, and there's more cards, RNG plays way more of a factor in Spire 2 than I personally ever feel it did in 1. It feels less when I lose like "♥♥♥♥, guess I really did need to pick up card I didn't want for this specific fight', or 'guess I needed to avoid elites', and more like 'guess I needed a better ancient relic, or to just never fight anything ever until the boss and win with health.' Which I think is fundamentally flawed for a game like this. The main fix to this in Spire 1 was shops. If you spent your gold wisely, because of the size of the card pool and all the other factors, you would always find something at least useful in a shop, but in this game, the relics are more expensive, you are more likely to brick a shop, and somehow they do just feel worse than in 1, in a lot of ways I can feel but I'm not sure I can articulate that makes them feel less like a bailout when your run is going bad, although they still serve that purpose but just not as well. I also think the difficulty curve is kind of bad. This was also a problem in Spire 1, where basically Act 2 was the hardest by far, but in Spire 2 it's worse because Act 2 is still ridiculously difficult, but now Act 1 is even harder so scaling up for it is very difficult as well. And act 3 is kind of a cakewalk because 1 and 2 are such a gauntlet I rarely feel like I'm weak enough by 3 for it to be a challenge, as if I was going to be in that position, I probably lost by then. Act 1 needs to be a little easier, just things hitting for slightly less damage or something. Act 2 could probably do with being easier, I'm thinking in a very specific way though, like Hunter-Killer having a capped debuff stack that increases during the fight and Prism having less health (he has comparable health to act 1 bosses, what the heck is even that).

As much as I want to like the game, as of today, I don't recommend this game as a solo experience (multiplayer is fun though). Most of the changes to the game these past few months have felt like the devs are actively trying to increase the amount of frustration there is in any given run, and the best way to deal with most mechanics is ignore them and end the encounter in less than 4 turns. Every enemy on every floor feels like a differently flavoured damage race, instead of an active interplay between the enemy and your deck. Worse yet, a lot of the fights that feel like they would reward a more consistent deck end up either getting changed in the beta branch (e.g. Skulking Colony) or have some sort of scaling mechanic in a fight where you're asked to deal with 20+ damage per turn regularly (e.g. Phantasmal Killer). Slay 2 is quite a fast paced game on average (at least compared to its predecessor), but it doesn't feel like an organic change of pace. Rather, it's because if the player doesn't have a fast enough deck, they just get crushed. Character decks feel very interesting, and synergies feel satisfying, but the fun I derive from actually playing a fight out gets sapped by numerous mechanics that feel overly punishing, especially to certain characters and archetypes (e.g. Vantom, Hunter Killer, Entomancer, new Infested Prism, 2 Chompers, Aeonglass, etc.). Further, because enemies are overly punishing to slower decks, the player is heavily incentivised to have a very slim deck for consistency, which means less opportunity to take more cards for fun and branch out to try new cards. This is on top of the devs nerfing the ability of the player to draw cards basically every time they make a change. Infinites were a problem that feel like they got addressed pretty quickly, and rightly so, but now it just feels like it's intended design to just regularly dead draw if the size of the player's deck is any more than 20 cards. More enemies have debilitating punishes to playing certain cards, many enemies regularly status your deck, and all of them punish you for not actively spending resources on them. Solutions to encounters feel much more one-dimensional than in Slay 1. Hunter Killer's a great example--if you don't have a Hulk Smash card or consistent debuff cycling, it's incredibly difficult to make progress on it. Oftentime even having a power card that increases your Strength and Dex doesn't feel enough. This is all to say that many encounters in Slay 2 range from difficult to simply unfun to interact with. Combined with the overall increased power in Event nodes, most of my runs have boiled down to avoiding fighting after Act 1 as much as possible, and fighting only 2~3 elites per run. Hallways are significantly more punishing than they are in Slay 1, card rewards after Act 1 feel much less valuable, and gold ironically feels less valuable because you need so much more of it to have a good shop. Relics on average feels much, much less satisfying to obtain and play with than Slay 1. Many strong relics in Slay 1 that have come back have bumped up a rarity (Nunchaku, Pen Nib, Art of War, Kunai/Shuriken, Meat on the Bone, Mummified Hand, etc.). The majority of new relics just don't feel like they've bridged the power gap either (Book of Five Rings, Festive Popper, Lucky Fysh, Beating Remnant, Tuning Fork, Sparkling Rouge, Reptile Trinket, etc.). Along with the fact that card rewards in general feel less satisfying as the player skips the vast majority of them on successful runs, it's often good practice to just avoid Elites altogether, as they're inconsistent power spikes at best for the amount of resources spent to fight them. What felt like the most engaging part of runs in Slay 1 became a point of avoidance, and since the launch of Early Access, the quality of the relic pool has only felt worse (Permafrost an Uncommon relic now?). I understand that this is an Early Access game and that all of this can change. And within the first month, it definitely looked that way, as a lot of the game was changing quite quickly. However, now that updates have slowed down, and the direction of the game seems to be more set in stone, I can't recommend sticking with this game until further notice. Slay 2 had a wonderful honeymoon period (and honestly still does whenever I boot up multiplayer with friends), but the singleplayer experience feels to be falling more and more from the golden standard that Slay 1 set. This was really just a Slay the Spire 1 recommendation in disguise. The more I play Slay 2, the more I crave Slay 1 instead. After 1500+ hours in it (Steam + mobile), I still love spamming runs in that game and trying to improve my 40% winrate on Silent A20H, but I feel no such motivation to grind to improve in Slay 2, especially when I feel like the game is degrading in quality.
